sources.finding: Checks display pass/fail/pending/skipped, source, timing and links for the PR current head commit; opening Checks or a new head refreshes GitHub data. PR comments appear below checks. Requires a selected GitHub account, PR and configured checks.

sources.title: Emdash Library sections
sources.finding: Library saves reusable prompts for new or existing conversations, installs/creates skills and configures MCP servers. Remote configuration is scoped to that machine and is not automatically copied from the laptop.

sources.title: Emdash Create an automation; Review runs
sources.finding: Scheduled runs select name, project, cron, prompt, agent and workspace. History shows timing, status and errors with associated task/conversation links. Runs can become regular tasks. Pausing stops future schedules.

sources.title: Emdash Supported providers; Feature support; Remote agents
sources.locator: Supported providers; Feature support; Remote agents
sources.finding: Classic names Pi and Grok among its 35 CLI providers. Auto-approve skips file-operation permission prompts for the providers that support it; resume/hooks vary by provider. Credentials and installation must exist on the execution machine; per-agent/machine model and effort preferences are remembered.

sources.title: Emdash homepage
sources.locator: Hero and 'All your coding agents in one place'; 'Get early access' form
sources.finding: Emdash 2.0 is an early-access team product that runs agents on the user's infrastructure or Emdash cloud with the user's own subscriptions and models; no prices are shown.

sources.title: emdash LICENSE.md

sources.title: Emdash Claude Code auth status check
sources.locator: packages/plugins/src/agents/impl/claude/auth.ts lines 17-33 and 46-56 (claudeAuthStatus, accountFromAuthStatus), release v1.2.11 commit 9346e91
sources.finding: Emdash treats Claude Code as authenticated when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set or when the installed claude CLI reports a signed-in account through its own auth status, including an OAuth account; Emdash holds no model credentials of its own.

sources.title: Emdash Providers docs
sources.locator: Supported Providers, Remote agents and Adding a Provider sections (last updated 2026-10-17)
sources.finding: Emdash detects installed provider CLIs on PATH; some CLIs need their own account authentication before Emdash can run them, and on remote machines the user installs and authenticates the CLI there.

sources.title: Emdash Antigravity support at v1.2.11
sources.finding: Emdash Classic v1.2.11 detects agy or antigravity and builds runnable Antigravity commands with initial prompts, models, permission flags and conversation resume.

sources.title: Emdash: apps/emdash-desktop/src/core/services/app-db/node/schema.ts
sources.locator: App database; packages/core/src runtime manifests and API schemas; apps/emdash-desktop/src/main; packages/plugins/src/agents/registry.ts
sources.finding: The scoped open-source desktop app persists projects, workspaces, conversations, linked external issues and automations. It supplies local/SSH workspaces with worktrees, not a separate native issue store. The desktop entry and runtime manifests contain no released web/native-phone client, standalone end-user CLI, managed vendor worker, container/VM provisioner, product agent coordinator role or multi-human account/role/SSO prompting service. Agent registry is statically registered. Emdash 2.0 hosted/team early access is a separate component.

sources.title: Emdash Classic complete supported providers
sources.locator: Supported Providers table (35 CLIs); matched pinned packages/plugins/src/agents/registry.ts
sources.finding: The complete Classic supported-provider list contains 35 coding-agent CLIs, including Antigravity, Pi and Grok, and omits Gemini CLI and Aider. The pinned registry registers the same fixed provider implementations; this is distinct from a list of example model names.

sources.title: Emdash Claude provider-key authentication
sources.locator: claudeAuthStatus: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY detection before native auth status
sources.finding: Classic detects authenticated Claude Code from the user ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable before querying native CLI authentication. Model API billing remains with the user provider account; the ADE does not resell the key usage.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Tasks
sources.locator: Creating a Task; Worktrees; After Starting
sources.finding: A task starts from a branch, issue or pull request with a name (or generated name) and a provider; no preset is required. By default each task gets its own git worktree and branch; worktrees can be disabled or an existing workspace used. Saved conversations and running processes have different lifetimes; tmux keeps terminal and TUI-agent sessions.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Providers
sources.locator: Supported Providers; Feature Support; Remote agents
sources.finding: 35 detected agent CLIs. Resume, hooks (working, awaiting input, done) and auto-approve are each supported by a listed subset of providers. Some provider CLIs require account authentication or product access before Emdash can run them. Remote agents must be installed and authenticated on the remote host; preferences are remembered per agent and machine; Chat UI or TUI is chosen in the agent selector.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Passing Issues
sources.locator: Create from an Issue; Supported Trackers; Connecting Your Tracker
sources.finding: Tasks can be created from Linear, Asana, Monday.com, Trello, GitHub, Jira, GitLab, Plane, Forgejo, Featurebase, Plain or Notion issues. The linked issue stays attached and inserted context includes provider, identifier, title, URL, description, status, assignees and project; the generated context can be reviewed or edited before sending. Trackers connect with personal API keys or tokens; GitHub uses the project's GitHub account.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Project Settings
sources.locator: What you can configure; Share settings with your team; Project environment variables; Lifecycle scripts
sources.finding: Per-project GitHub account, worktree directory, remotes, tmux, agent git credentials, environment variables, preserve patterns (copy .env-style files into new tasks), shell setup and prepare/setup/run/teardown scripts. Scripts, preserve patterns and shell setup can be shared through .emdash.json; for remote projects they run on the remote machine. Env vars are personal settings; credentials should not go in a committed .emdash.json. Run script logs show in the terminal drawer; EMDASH_PORT and a Docker Compose example support services.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Installation
sources.finding: Emdash runs agents through their official CLIs. Users add a local project, clone a GitHub repository or connect a remote machine. Emdash works locally without signing in or connecting GitHub; GitHub and tracker integrations are optional.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Automations
sources.locator: Create an automation; Where it runs; Review runs
sources.finding: Automations run an agent prompt on a cron schedule in a project's new worktree, existing workspace or repository root. For remote projects the Workspace Server owns scheduling and execution and the desktop need not stay connected; a stopped machine cannot run. Run history shows timing, status and errors.

sources.title: Emdash docs: GitHub Accounts
sources.locator: Connect GitHub; Manage Accounts; Project Selection; Git authentication
sources.finding: Multiple GitHub accounts can be connected (Emdash account/OAuth, GitHub CLI import or device flow) and each project selects one for issues, pull requests (create, list, merge), checks and repository creation. Agent git credentials can use that account, system credentials or none.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Remote Development
sources.finding: The Emdash UI stays on the laptop; repositories, worktrees, agents, terminals, lifecycle scripts, search and scheduled automations run on the SSH machine through the Workspace Server. Agent CLIs and credentials must be installed and authenticated on that machine. A banner advertises Emdash 2.0 early access.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Manage Machines
sources.locator: System; Workspaces and conversations; Agents, MCP and skills; Automations
sources.finding: The System tab shows connection, resource usage and dependencies and installs, starts, restarts, shuts down or updates the Workspace Server. A Conversations tab lists agent sessions on the machine. Subscription readings are in Settings, Usage. Closing the desktop does not stop remote automations.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Remote Projects and Tasks
sources.locator: Open a project; Create a task; Agents, files and tools; Previews and reconnects
sources.finding: Remote projects can pick, clone or create a GitHub repository. Tasks use a new worktree, existing workspace or repository root; tasks in the same directory share files. Local files and pasted images are uploaded into remote terminals; chat attachments are stored on the target machine. Tmux keeps processes across disconnects but not a reboot.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Connect a Machine
sources.finding: Add a machine in Settings, Machines with an SSH alias or host details (password, key or agent auth), test it, then install or start the Workspace Runtime from the System tab and add a remote project. Hosts need SSH, Git and the development tools.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Tmux Sessions
sources.finding: Tmux keeps terminal and TUI-agent processes and history on the host across closed views or lost SSH, but not through a host reboot or explicit termination. Chat UI history and provider resume are separate.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Diff View
sources.finding: The Pull Requests section shows PR files, commits, checks, comments and merge state for the task branch. Commit offers Commit, Commit & Push or Commit & Create PR; the footer shows fetch, pull, push and publish actions.

sources.title: Emdash docs: CI/CD Checks
sources.finding: The Checks tab lists GitHub check runs for the PR head with status, source, duration and links, and shows PR comments below them.

sources.title: Emdash docs: In-App Browser
sources.finding: An in-app browser previews task dev servers. Remote previews forward the remote port to the laptop automatically or through Forward Port with an optional local port; no tunnel lifetime or access control is documented.

sources.title: Emdash docs: File Editor
sources.finding: The file editor offers syntax highlighting, find/replace, tabs and language intelligence (definitions, references, diagnostics) in local and SSH workspaces.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Keyboard Shortcuts
sources.finding: Default shortcuts such as Cmd+N create task, Cmd+J terminal drawer, Cmd+Shift+B browser and Cmd+Shift+1 changes panel; most can be rebound in Settings.

sources.title: Emdash docs: MCP Servers
sources.locator: Adding a Server from the Catalog; Editing and Removing; Catalog Servers
sources.finding: MCP servers are added from a 54-server catalog (including Context7 and Exa) or as custom stdio/http servers, with required credentials entered in the modal, and synced into each selected agent's native config. Remove deletes a server from all agents.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Prompts
sources.finding: Saved prompts can be edited or deleted from the library and inserted into task conversations.

sources.title: Emdash docs: Skills
sources.finding: Installed skills can be uninstalled, removing them from ~/.agentskills and the agent symlinks.

sources.title: What's next for Emdash
sources.finding: Emdash 2.0 (coding agents for whole teams) is in early access with a work-email waitlist. The current desktop app is renamed Emdash Classic; it stays open source and keeps getting fixes. No end date is given.

sources.title: Emdash Classic changelog
sources.finding: v1.2.10: long workspace operations no longer fail after 30 seconds; credential tokens and environment values stay out of process arguments. v1.2.9 adds GitLab repository creation and merge request workflows. Retrieved 2026-11-21, the page's newest entry is v1.2.10.

sources.title: Emdash v1.2.11 release notes
sources.finding: Project Git credentials apply to Emdash's own push, pull and fetch; users can join the Emdash 2.0 waitlist from the sidebar.

sources.title: Emdash v1.2.12 release notes
sources.finding: Waitlist signups go to emdash.com; importing data from Emdash v0 runs in one transaction.

sources.title: Emdash Workspace Server package and repository license (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: The Workspace Server daemon lives in apps/workspace-server of the same repository, declares Apache-2.0 and has no separate license file; the root LICENSE.md is Apache-2.0 (General Action, Inc.).

sources.title: Emdash desktop source: bounded billing search (v1.2.13)
sources.locator: search of apps/ and packages/ for stripe, checkout, purchase, billing and credits
sources.finding: No purchase, billing or credit-sale code exists in the Classic desktop or Workspace Server; credit matches are wire flow control and an MCP catalog description.

sources.title: Emdash archiveTask and restoreTask (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Archiving sets archivedAt and reaps the task's tmux session and agent process while keeping the worktree and session id; restoreTask clears archivedAt so the task can resume.

sources.title: Emdash search service (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: The app search index holds projects, tasks (with branch) and conversations, updated on create, rename, archive and delete; archived tasks leave the index.

sources.title: Emdash automation scheduler (v1.2.13)
sources.locator: DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS line 17; queueDueRuns and worker loop lines 206-264
sources.finding: Due automation runs are marked queued and started only while running workers are below maxConcurrentRuns (default 4); others wait in the queue.

sources.title: Emdash merge UI state and footer (v1.2.13)
sources.locator: canBypass line 27; BLOCKED and pending-check states; merge-footer.tsx bypass checkbox
sources.finding: For GitHub PRs that are blocked, behind or waiting on checks, Emdash offers merging only after ticking 'Merge without waiting for requirements to be met (bypass rules)'; GitLab gets no bypass. Whether the bypass succeeds is decided by the Git host. A bounded search of source-control, github and agent/issue plugin code for deployment found no deployment status tracking.

sources.title: Emdash diff line comments (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Draft line comments attach to working-tree, PR or commit diffs and can be inserted into an agent conversation through the Diff comments mention.

sources.title: Emdash provider usage probes (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Usage probes report account, plan and usage windows with percent used and reset time; probes are implemented only for Claude Code and Codex.

sources.title: Emdash v0 data import (v1.2.13)
sources.locator: legacy-port importers: projects, tasks, conversations, ssh-connections
sources.finding: The desktop detects an Emdash v0 database and imports its projects, tasks, conversations and SSH connections.

sources.title: Emdash issue provider capability (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Issue providers implement listIssues, searchIssues and optional getIssue only; a bounded search of the provider implementations found no create, update, comment, transition or POST/PATCH/PUT calls.

sources.title: Emdash per-provider settings (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Settings are stored per host and provider: Chat UI (ACP) keeps the provider's own option values; TUI (PTY) keeps an autoApprove flag that defaults to false.

sources.title: Emdash conversation model (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Each conversation in a task has its own providerId, pty or acp transport, session id, model, agentStatus and agentStatusSeen flag, so a task can hold conversations with different agents.

sources.title: Emdash ACP chat store (v1.2.13)
sources.locator: permissionQueue and queuedPrompts; edit/delete queued prompt
sources.finding: Chat UI queues prompts sent while the agent is busy (editable and deletable) and surfaces provider permission requests in a queue the user answers.

sources.title: Emdash agent status and attention events (v1.2.13)
sources.finding: Agent status is idle, working, awaiting-input, error or completed; permission, idle and elicitation hook notifications count as attention and drive needs-attention sounds and notifications.
